title: Autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Michael Chen
release_notes:
- Add autotune defaults for batching and caching to reduce per-token unit cost for common workloads.
- Introduce curated quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit safe) with compatibility labels per model family.
- Expose unit-econ tooling in Console and API for per-route cost projections and suggested config changes.
description: Context: ENG-2345/ENG-2399. This PR wires together three pieces of cost-optimization automation: (1) autotuned defaults for batching and KV caching per-model/route based on historical latency/load traces, (2) curated quantization profiles that are safe-by-default with compatibility labels and fallback behavior, and (3) a first-pass unit-econ tooling surface that surfaces projected per-token cost and suggested config changes in the Console and via the internal API. Motivation: customers frequently ask for guidance on batch/cache settings and quantization tradeoffs; manual tuning is error-prone and costly. This change reduces OPEX by enabling safer defaults and automated recommendations while preserving latency SLOs. What changed (high level): commits implement autotune heuristics + scheduler hooks, add quant profiles and model-matrix metadata, extend the routing/config API to accept "optimizations.autotune=true", add Console UI hooks and backend endpoints for unit economics projections, and add end-to-end integration tests and benchmarks. See linked Linear tickets for evaluation criteria. Checklist: - [x] Autotune core heuristics implemented and unit tested - [x] Quantization profiles added for LLaMA2/Baichuan/Redwood-v1 families - [x] API and Console surfaces for unit-econ projections - [x] Integration + perf tests + CI green - [x] Docs and changelog entries updated
